entry.title: Persistent Data Structure - Segment Tree
entry.content:
Persistent DataStructure - Segment Tree

A persistent data structure is a data structure that always preservesthe previous version of itself when it is modified. Such data structuresare effectively immutable, as their operations do not update thestructure in place, but instead always yield a new updatedstructure.

You should be familiar with basic segment trees before reading thispost.

Problem Statement

Persistent SegmentTree

You need to maintain an arrayaawith a length ofNN,supporting the following two operations:

  1. Modify the value at a certain position in some historicalversion
  2. Query the value at a certain position in some historicalversion

In addition, each operation creates a new version. The version numberis the index of the current operation, starting from 1, while version 0represents the initial state of the array.

For operation 2, the newly created version is completely identical tothe version being queried, with no modifications made. In other words,the version generated by a query operation is simply a copy of theversion that was queried.

Input Format

The first line contains two positive integersNNandMM,representing the length of the array and the number of operations,respectively.

The second line containsNNintegers, where theii-thinteger isaia_i.

The nextMMlines each contain either 3 or 4 integers, representing one of thefollowing two operations. Suppose the current operation is theii-thoperation:

  1. For operation 1, the format isv 1 p c, meaning that based on versionvv,setapa_ptocc.
  2. For operation 2, the format is v 2 p,meaning that we query the value ofapa_pin versionvv.Note that this operation also creates a new version that isidentical to versionvv.
  • 1≤N,M≤1061 \le N, M \le 10^6
  • 1≤p≤n1 \le p \le n
  • −109≤ai,c≤109-10^9 \le a_i, c \le 10^9

Copy the path

It is not hard to see that the limit is not the time complexity, butthe space complexity. If we build a separate segment tree for everyversion, we will definitely exceed the memory limit.

If we change the value of a leaf node, only the node on the path fromthe root to that leaf node would change, so that we only want to copythe path instead of creating a new tree. This is the idea behind apersistent segment tree.

You can find that a new root corresponds to a new version, anddifferent versions share some nodes. Because of that, we cannot use(idx * 2) and (idx * 2 + 1) to calculate theleft son and right son.

Build The Tree

Use the Structure to maintain node information:

The build function is similar to an ordinary segment tree. The onlydifference is that each node is assigned a unique index using++cnt.

Here, rt is a reference to the nodeindex, so its type should be int &.

After calling build(t[rt].ls, ...), the newly allocatednode index will be written directly into the parent node’sls field.

Update the Tree

Let update(idx, l, r, q, val) denote the followingoperation: based on the interval[l,r][l,r]represented by the old node idx, update the value atposition q to val, and return the index of theroot node of the modified subtree.

At each level of recursion, we first execute:

This only copies the three integers stored in the current node. Itdoes not recursively copy the entire subtree. At this point, the newnode and the old node temporarily point to the same left and rightchildren.

Next, we recurse only into the side that contains q -the target path that we want to copy, and connect the returned new childindex to current. The child index on the other side remainsunchanged, which allows the two versions to share unchangedsubtrees.

Throughout the recursion, we maintain the two invariants:

  • the old node is never modified
  • in the new subtree, only the value at position q ischanged.

At the leaf node, we directly assign the new value. As the recursionreturns, we reconnect the copied nodes along the path, eventuallyobtaining the root of the new version.

It’s not enough to copy only the leaf node, since the leaf’s parentmust point to the new leaf, and the parent’s parent must also point tothe new child. Therefore, the entire path from the leaf up to the rootmust be copied.

Query

Just head out from the root node, choose the left subtree or theright subtree according to the query position, and return the value whenyou reach the target leaf node.

Attention: a query also creates a new version. Since no valueschange, the new version can share the entire tree.

Space Complexity

The initial segment tree hasnnleaf nodes. Since every internal node has exactly two children, the treecontains a total of2n−12n-1nodes.

Suppose there areuuupdate operations. Each update copies at most⌈log⁡2n⌉+1\lceil \log_2 n\rceil+1nodes, including the root and the leaf. Therefore, an upper bound on thetotal number of nodes is

(2n−1)+u(⌈log⁡2n⌉+1). (2n-1)+u\bigl(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+1\bigr).

Forn,m≤106n,m\le 10^6,each update creates at most 21 new nodes, so the total number of nodesis less than2.3×1072.3\times10^7.In the implementation below, we reserve MAXN * 23 nodes forthe node pool.

The node indices, version indices, and point values in the range[−109,109][-10^9,10^9]all fit within a 32-bit int. In a typical environment wherean int takes 4 bytes and each node takes 12 bytes, the nodepool uses about 263 MiB. Together with the base androot arrays, the three arrays use about 271 MiB in total.Since there are no range-sum queries in this problem, there is no needto use long long for every field.

More precisely, the complexities are:

  • Building the initial tree:O(n)O(n).
  • Each update or query:O(1+log⁡n)O(1+\log n).
  • Total space:O(n+m+u(1+log⁡n))O\bigl(n+m+u(1+\log n)\bigr),where the root array itself takesO(m)O(m)space.

In most cases, we simply write the complexity of each operation asO(log⁡n)O(\log n),and the total space complexity asO(n+mlog⁡n)O(n+m\log n).

Whenn=1n=1,an update still copies one leaf node.

entry.title: Convex Hull Trick
entry.content:
Convex Hull Trick

The Convex Hull Trick can speed up a dynamic programming transitionby treating each previous state as a line. In this post, we will derivethis transformation for a partitioning problem and explain how amonotonic deque reduces the running time fromO(n2)O(n^2)toO(n)O(n).

Problem analysis

Starting with a quadratic DP

Consider HNOI2008 ToyPacking.

There arennitems arranged in a line. Theii-thitem has lengthcic_i,and we need to partition the items into contiguous groups. For a group[l,r][l,r],the cost is

(r−l+∑k=lrck−L)2,\left(r-l+\sum_{k=l}^{r}c_k-L\right)^2,

whereLLis a constant. The termr−lr-laccounts for the one-unit gap between each pair of adjacent items in thegroup. Our goal is to minimize the total cost of all groups.

The constraints are

1≤n≤5×104,1≤L,ci≤107.1\le n\le 5\times 10^4,\qquad 1\le L,c_i\le 10^7.

Letfif_idenote the minimum total cost of partitioning the firstiiitems. Define the prefix sums as

Si=∑k=1ick,S0=f0=0.S_i=\sum_{k=1}^{i}c_k,\qquad S_0=f_0=0.

If the final group contains itemsj+1j+1throughii,its total length isSi−Sj+i−j−1S_i-S_j+i-j-1.Considering every possible starting position of this final group givesthe recurrence

fi=min0≤j<i{fj+(i−(j+1)+Si−Sj−L)2}=min0≤j<i{fj+(Si−Sj+i−j−1−L)2}.\begin{aligned}f_i&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+\left(i-(j+1)+S_i-S_j-L\right)^2\right\}\\&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+\left(S_i-S_j+i-j-1-L\right)^2\right\}.\end{aligned}

This straightforward solution checks every previous state for eachii,resulting in anO(n2)O(n^2)algorithm.

Rewriting the transition

Expanding the square allows us to separate the terms that depend onlyoniifrom those involvingjj.

Letai=Si+ia_i=S_i+i.We can then write

Si−Sj+i−j−1−L=ai−aj−L−1.S_i-S_j+i-j-1-L=a_i-a_j-L-1.

Now letxi=ai−L−1x_i=a_i-L-1.The recurrence becomes

fi=min0≤j<i{fj+(xi−aj)2}=xi2+min0≤j<i{−2ajxi+fj+aj2}.\begin{aligned}f_i&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+(x_i-a_j)^2\right\}\\&=x_i^2+\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{-2a_jx_i+f_j+a_j^2\right\}.\end{aligned}

For a fixedii,the termxi2x_i^2is the same for every candidatejj,so it can be moved outside the minimum.

Interpreting each state as aline

For each previous statejj,define a line

ℓj(x)=kjx+bj,\ell_j(x)=k_jx+b_j,

where

kj=−2aj=−2(Sj+j),bj=fj+aj2=fj+(Sj+j)2.k_j=-2a_j=-2(S_j+j),\qquadb_j=f_j+a_j^2=f_j+(S_j+j)^2.

Computingfif_inow requires finding the minimum value among these lines atx=xix=x_i,then addingxi2x_i^2:

fi=xi2+min0≤j<iℓj(xi).f_i=x_i^2+\min_{0\le j<i}\ell_j(x_i).

Once we have computedfif_i,we can construct its line and make it available to subsequent states. Wequery before inserting the new line because only states withj<ij<iare valid candidates.

Maintaining the candidatelines

To speed up the transition, we discard lines that cannot improve theanswer to any future query. However, we cannot keep only the line thatis currently optimal: a different line may become optimal as the querycoordinate changes.

We will use a deque under two conditions:

  • Lines are inserted in strictly decreasing order of slope.
  • Query coordinates are nondecreasing.

The first condition lets us remove redundant lines from the back ofthe deque. The second lets us discard lines from the front as we answerqueries.

Adding a new line

Consider three linesPP,QQ,andRRwith strictly decreasing slopes:

kP>kQ>kR.k_P>k_Q>k_R.

Thexx-coordinateof the intersection ofPPandQQis

X(P,Q)=bQ−bPkP−kQ.X(P,Q)=\frac{b_Q-b_P}{k_P-k_Q}.

ForQQto be no higher than bothPPandRR,we need

X(P,Q)≤x≤X(Q,R).X(P,Q)\le x\le X(Q,R).

Therefore, if

X(P,Q)≥X(Q,R),X(P,Q)\ge X(Q,R),

thenQQis never strictly better than bothPPandRR.When the two intersection coordinates are equal, all three lines meet atthe same point, soQQcan still be removed without changing the minimum value.

When inserting a new lineRR,we apply this test to the last two lines in the deque andRR.If the middle line is redundant, we remove it from the back and repeatthe test. We then appendRR.

Answering queries

Suppose the first two lines in the deque arePPandQQ,withkP>kQk_P>k_Q.If, at the current query coordinatexx,

Q(x)≤P(x),Q(x)\le P(x),

thenQQremains no higher thanPPfor every later coordinate. To see why, letx′≥xx'\ge x.We have

Q(x′)−P(x′)=Q(x)−P(x)+(kQ−kP)(x′−x)≤0.Q(x')-P(x')=Q(x)-P(x)+(k_Q-k_P)(x'-x)\le 0.

We can therefore removePPfrom the front of the deque. We repeat this comparison until only oneline remains or the first line is better than the second at the currentcoordinate.

The insertion step keeps the intersection coordinates of consecutivelines in increasing order. This ensures that, once the front comparisonsstop, the first line gives the minimum value among all remainingcandidates.

Applying the optimization

Returning to our problem, we have

ai+1−ai=ci+1+1>0.a_{i+1}-a_i=c_{i+1}+1>0.

Thus,aia_iis strictly increasing. The inserted slopeskj=−2ajk_j=-2a_jare strictly decreasing, and the query coordinatesxi=ai−L−1x_i=a_i-L-1are strictly increasing. Both conditions required by the deque aresatisfied.

Each line is inserted once and removed at most once, from either end.Although a single operation may remove several lines, there are onlyO(n)O(n)removals over the entire algorithm. The total running time is thereforeO(n)O(n),withO(n)O(n)space in the worst case.

Understanding theimplementation

Matching the code to therecurrence

The implementation below uses an equivalent arrangement of the samerecurrence. It keeps the query coordinate ataia_iand includes the constantL+1L+1in each line instead.

Define

tj=aj+L+1.t_j=a_j+L+1.

Then

fi=min0≤j<i{fj+(ai−tj)2}=ai2+min0≤j<i{(−2tj)ai+fj+tj2}.\begin{aligned}f_i&=\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{f_j+(a_i-t_j)^2\right\}\\&=a_i^2+\min_{0\le j<i}\left\{(-2t_j)a_i+f_j+t_j^2\right\}.\end{aligned}

The code therefore uses the following quantities:

CodeMeaning
s[i]The prefix sumSiS_i.
f[i]The minimum costfif_i.
x = s[i] + iThe current query coordinateaia_i.
tThe valuetj=aj+L+1t_j=a_j+L+1for the state whose line is being constructed.
line.firThe slope−2tj-2t_j.
line.secThe interceptfj+tj2f_j+t_j^2.

Here, fir and sec are macros forfirst and second. The deque stores each lineas a pair containing its slope and intercept. Since addingL+1L+1preserves the order of theaja_jvalues, the slopes still decrease and the query coordinates stillincrease.

Initializing the deque

The initial candidate is statej=0j=0,wherea0=f0=0a_0=f_0=0.Therefore,t0=L+1t_0=L+1,and its line is

y=−2(L+1)x+(L+1)2.y=-2(L+1)x+(L+1)^2.

This explains the initialization t = L + 1 andq.push_back({-2 * t, t * t}). State00represents placing all of the firstiiitems into a single group. The global arrays are zero-initialized,providing s[0] = f[0] = 0.

Querying the minimum

The helper value(line, x) evaluates a line at thecurrent coordinate. In the first while loop, ifq[1] is no higher than q[0], the first linecan be removed permanently. The <= comparison alsohandles ties: the second line has a smaller slope and is at least asgood for every future query.

After this loop, q.front() gives the minimum line value,so the assignment f[i] = x*x + value(q.front(), x) computesthe current DP state.

Inserting the current state

After computing f[i], the code setst = x + L + 1. Since x = a_i, this is exactlyti=ai+L+1t_i=a_i+L+1.The new line R has slope−2ti-2t_iand interceptfi+ti2f_i+t_i^2.

The helper check(A, B, C) determines whether the middleline B is redundant. It tests

X(A,B)≥X(B,C).X(A,B)\ge X(B,C).

BecausekA>kB>kCk_A>k_B>k_C,both denominators in the intersection formulas are positive. We cantherefore compare the intersections by cross multiplication:

(bB−bA)(kB−kC)≥(kA−kB)(bC−bB).(b_B-b_A)(k_B-k_C)\ge(k_A-k_B)(b_C-b_B).

This is the expression used in check, avoiding divisionwhen comparing intersection coordinates. The second whileloop removes redundant lines from the back, andq.push_back(R) makes the new state available to futurequeries.

entry.title: 费马小定理
entry.content:
取模 & 费马小定理

取模的性质

(a+b)mod⁡p=(amod⁡p+bmod⁡p)mod⁡p(a + b) \bmod p = (a \bmod p + b \bmod p) \bmod p

(a−b)mod⁡p=(amod⁡p−bmod⁡p)mod⁡p(a - b) \bmod p = (a \bmod p - b \bmod p) \bmod p

(a*b)mod⁡p=(amod⁡p*bmod⁡p)mod⁡p(a * b) \bmod p = (a \bmod p * b \bmod p) \bmod p

abmod⁡p=(amod⁡p)bmod⁡pa^b \bmod p = (a \bmod p)^b \bmod p

除法没有相关性质，因此下面引入费马小定理与乘法逆元

若pp为素数，对于任何整数a，ap≡a(mod⁡p)a^p \equiv a \pmod{p}

为方便在取模意义下计算除法，为此引入乘法逆元：

若bb是aa在模pp意义下的乘法逆元，那么$ab $

那么

$ (x a) p = (x * b) p$

因此可应用乘法性质

由费马小定理易得 ：aa在模pp意义下的乘法逆元为ap−2a^{p-2}（p为素数）

一般计算逆元可用快速幂

一些情况可能会用到线性求 1-n 的逆元或线性求 1-n 阶乘的逆元
